title: Three-act screenplay analysis
summary: Urban has a strong moral engine, but the opening can make his active choice clearer.

criteria.label: Dramatic Energy
criteria.description: How strongly the moment pulls the audience forward.

criteria.label: Stakes
criteria.description: How clearly the audience understands what can be lost or gained.

criteria.label: Character Agency
criteria.description: How clearly a character's choice drives the story.

actSegments.title: The Offer
actSegments.synopsis: Urban is introduced through need, skill, and the first failed patronage attempt.

critique.summary: The act has pressure, but Urban's active choice can arrive sooner.
strengths: The premise gives craft a moral consequence.
concerns: The opening pressure can feel external before Urban's want is explicit.

evidence.text: The first scene shows pressure before it clearly dramatizes Urban choosing a path.

suggestions: Make Urban's decision pressure visible before the act moves to negotiation.

actSegments.title: The Patron
actSegments.synopsis: Urban enters a world that can fund his ambition and shrink his moral distance.

critique.summary: The act gains scale when resources meet ambition.
strengths: The patron relationship naturally raises stakes.
concerns: Urban's self-justification should be tested by visible human cost.

evidence.text: The patron scene turns skill into political consequence.

suggestions: Let a scene force Urban to defend his bargain in human terms.

actSegments.title: The Sound
actSegments.synopsis: The weapon works, and Urban must face the meaning of success.

critique.summary: The final act has scale and consequence; the strongest version makes recognition unavoidable.
strengths: The climax naturally ties invention to empire-level cost.
concerns: Urban's inner recognition needs a clear dramatic expression.

evidence.text: The wall sequence shows the weapon succeeding at a human cost.

suggestions: Give Urban a concrete moment of recognition before the final consequence lands.

keyBeats.label: Hook
keyBeats.synopsis: The story opens on pressure created by Urban's craft.

critique.summary: The hook is forceful but can attach more tightly to Urban's choice.

evidence.text: The scene shows consequence before choice.

suggestions: Tie the opening image to a question about Urban's responsibility.

keyBeats.label: Inciting Incident
keyBeats.synopsis: The patronage offer makes the old path impossible.

critique.summary: The disruption is legible but not yet bound to a Scene strongly enough.

evidence.text: The opening establishes the pressure that makes the offer consequential.

suggestions: Make the offer's arrival a visible break from Urban's prior path.

keyBeats.label: First Plot Point
keyBeats.synopsis: Urban commits his craft to the patronage path.

critique.summary: The commitment is present and can become more explicitly chosen.

evidence.text: Urban moves from pressure toward the bargain.

suggestions: Stage the commitment as a choice among real alternatives.

keyBeats.label: First Pinch Point
keyBeats.synopsis: The patron demonstrates the cost of refusing power.

critique.summary: Opposition becomes concrete through the patron relationship.

evidence.text: The patron turns resources into leverage over Urban.

suggestions: Let the pressure threaten something Urban has already chosen to protect.

keyBeats.label: Midpoint
keyBeats.synopsis: Urban's apparent success reveals the scale of his compromise.

critique.summary: The reversal connects ambition to human cost.

evidence.text: The bargain expands from personal survival to political consequence.

suggestions: Make the new cost impossible for Urban to dismiss as abstract.

keyBeats.label: Second Pinch Point
keyBeats.synopsis: The patron closes off retreat as the weapon nears use.

critique.summary: Pressure rises while Urban's available choices narrow.

evidence.text: The patron relationship now carries irreversible consequence.

suggestions: Show the last viable exit before it disappears.

keyBeats.label: Second Plot Point
keyBeats.synopsis: Urban confronts the final use of his work.

critique.summary: The story moves cleanly into consequence.

evidence.text: The weapon reaches the wall and makes the moral question immediate.

suggestions: Give Urban one final action that reveals his answer.

keyBeats.label: Climax
keyBeats.synopsis: The weapon succeeds and forces recognition.

critique.summary: The external climax lands; Urban's decisive agency can be sharper.

evidence.text: The wall sequence makes success and harm inseparable.

suggestions: Make Urban's response alter the immediate outcome or relationship.

keyBeats.label: Resolution
keyBeats.synopsis: The screenplay has not yet separated aftermath from climax.

critique.summary: A distinct aftermath is not yet embodied by a current Scene.

evidence.text: The available ending Scene still carries the decisive action rather than a new state.

suggestions: Add or revise an aftermath Scene that shows what Urban now understands and chooses.

sceneGroups.title: The Sound That Opens Stone
sceneGroups.synopsis: The sequence frames the cost of the weapon before the bargain.

critique.summary: A strong pressure sequence with room for clearer agency.
strengths: The audience understands that the weapon matters.
concerns: The audience needs a sharper sense of Urban's immediate want.

evidence.text: The scene emphasizes result before decision.

suggestions: End the sequence on a question about responsibility, not only spectacle.

sceneAnalyses.synopsis: The cannon's impact establishes the cost of Urban's craft.

critique.summary: The scene is forceful but low on visible agency.
strengths: Immediate consequence gives the story scale.
concerns: Urban is defined by effect before choice.

evidence.text: The conflict is external before Urban's decision is dramatized.

suggestions: Add or revise a beat so Urban actively confronts what his craft enables.

sceneAnalyses.synopsis: The patron turns Urban's ambition into an enforceable bargain.

critique.summary: The bargain raises scale and moral pressure.
suggestions: Force Urban to name what he is accepting.

sceneAnalyses.synopsis: The weapon's success makes Urban's responsibility visible.

critique.summary: The consequence is powerful and needs a distinct aftermath.

evidence.text: The wall sequence joins achievement to harm.

suggestions: Separate the final decision from the state that follows it.

suggestedScenes.title: The Maker Calculates
suggestedScenes.purpose: Give Urban an active choice after the opening pressure.
suggestedScenes.synopsis: Urban privately weighs whether his craft can survive without patronage and chooses pursuit over retreat.
suggestedScenes.rationale: This makes the hook personal instead of only situational.

expectedCriterionChanges.reason: The audience sees Urban choose pressure rather than merely experience it.
